        except ValueError:
            held = None
        seed_used = isinstance(held, dict)
        fargs.update(seed_used=seed_used,
                     facts=call_facts_of(held if seed_used else {},
                                         rows_latest_per_item(shown(rows(lg, "f-notes")))
                                         if NOTES_PER_ITEM else shown(rows(lg, "f-notes")),
                                         st.get(SCREEN_KEY, "")))
        drows = sorted([int(r.get("seq") or 0), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""),
                        str(r.get("hash") or "")]
                       for r in shown(rows(lg, "f-dele")) if of_call(r, call, _SEED["sid"]))
        fargs["drows"] = drows
        hashes = sorted({h for _, _, h in drows if h})
        if hashes:
            emit([lstore([("f-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash", "body"],
                                           {"hash": {"in": hashes}}))],
                         "call-facts-blocks", "call_facts", json.dumps(fargs, sort_keys=True))])
        bodies = {}
    else:
        bodies = bodies_of(lg, "f-blocks")
    texts, order = {}, []
    for _, t, h in fargs.get("drows") or []:
        text = text_of(element_of(bodies.get(h)))
        if not text.strip():
            continue
        if t not in texts:
            texts[t] = []
            order.append(t)
        texts[t].append(text)
    delegations = [{"turn_id": t, "text": "\n".join(texts[t])} for t in order]
    emit([call_facts_answer(call, fargs.get("seed_used") is True, fargs.get("facts") or [],
                            delegations)])
if phase == "judge-write":
    if failed(lg) or str(hop.get("error_code") or ""):
        sys.stderr.write("curator/history: the ledger refused a %s write\n"
                         % (str(ctx.get("cur_call") or "") or "judge"))
    emit([])
if phase == "reread":
    if failed(lg):
        sys.stderr.write("curator/history: a reread mark was refused: %s\n"
                         % ", ".join(failed(lg)))
    emit([])

call_id = str(ctx.get("cur_call") or "")
try:
    carried = json.loads(str(ctx.get("cur_reason") or "") or "{}")
except Exception:
    carried = {}
name = str((carried or {}).get("tool") or "")
args = (carried or {}).get("args") or {}
if "r-soft" in lg and not args.get("soft"):
    # The window `./policy` keeps, read with a read's first step; it rides the
    # call's later steps in `args`.
    args["soft"] = next((str(r.get("value") or "") for r in rows(lg, "r-soft")), "")
READ_BUDGET = budget_chars(args.get("soft"), READ_SHARE)


def over_budget(size):
    return READ_BUDGET is not None and size > READ_BUDGET


def budget_said(extra):
    """`extra` and the budget it was measured by, when there is one."""
    return dict(extra, budget=READ_BUDGET) if READ_BUDGET is not None else dict(extra)
if not call_id or name not in ARGS:
    park("store answer in phase %r without its call -- dropped" % phase)
if audience_of(ROUND) is None:
    # The round rides the context through every ledger round trip; a store
    # answer that lost it on the way shows nothing of what was read (GH #925).
    sys.stderr.write("curator/history: a store answer in phase %s without its round\n" % phase)
    refuse(call_id, name, "missing_audience", NO_ROUND)
if failed(lg):
    # The ledger refusing a read is this hive's failure, not the model's: it is
    # said here and answered there, so the round the call belongs to closes.
    sys.stderr.write("curator/history: ledger refused %s in phase %s\n"
                     % (", ".join(failed(lg)), phase))
    refuse(call_id, name, "ledger_error", "the ledger refused the read; try again later")

if phase == "search-rows":
    first = within(args, rows(lg, "s-next"))
    if not first:
        finish_search(args)
    emit([page_bundle(args, first)])

if phase == "search-page":
    page = rows(lg, "s-page")
    nxt = rows(lg, "s-next")
    cut = scan_page(args, page, bodies_of(lg, "s-blocks"))
    args["pages"] = int(args.get("pages") or 0) + 1
    if cut:
        finish_search(args, cut_by=cut)
    if args.pop("planning", False):
        # The read the first hidden row asked for (OR-BD-74): every page
        # still to scan is planned out of it, the next one read with it.
        planned, tail = plan_of(args, nxt)
        later = planned[0] if planned else []
        args["plan"] = [[int(p[0].get("seq") or 0), len(p)] for p in planned[1:]]
        args["tail"] = tail
        more = True if planned else TAIL[tail]
    elif args.get("plan") is not None:
        later = within(args, nxt)
        more = (True if shown(later) else None) if args["plan"] else TAIL[args.get("tail")]
        args["plan"] = args["plan"][1:]
    else:
        later = within(args, nxt)
        more = ahead(args, nxt, later)
    settle(args, more)
    if not later:
        # Not reached (a page that goes on has a row); were it, the search
        # could not answer as the wall without hidden rows does.
        finish_cut(args)
    emit([page_bundle(args, later)])

if phase == "search-near":
    want = int(args.get("context") or 0) + NEAR_SPARE
    reach = [[near_reach(rows(lg, "%s%d" % (side, i)), want, want) for side in ("nb", "na")]
             for i in range(len(args["hits"]))]
    short_of = sum(x is None for pair in reach for x in pair)
    if short_of:
        # Hidden rows of the session beside a hit (OR-BD-86): that side is
        # read again up to its share of the row bound, so the window holds the
        # rows of the wall without them -- one ledger round trip more.
        wide = near_wide(short_of)
        if wide <= want:
            finish_cut(args)
        args["near"] = [[x or wide for x in pair] for pair in reach]
        emit([lstore(near_ops(args["hits"], 0, args["near"]), "search-near-more", call_id,
                     carry(name, args))])
    near_bodies(args, lg, None)

if phase == "search-near-more":
    want = int(args.get("context") or 0) + NEAR_SPARE
    for i, pair in enumerate(args["near"]):
        for j, side in enumerate(("nb", "na")):
            reach = near_reach(rows(lg, "%s%d" % (side, i)), pair[j], want)
            if reach is None:
                # The window lies past the share of the row bound: whether
                # and which rows the round may see stand there is open -- the
                # whole search answers in the cut form, the one bit.
                finish_cut(args)
            pair[j] = reach
    near_bodies(args, lg, args["near"])

if phase == "search-near-2":
    width = int(args.get("context") or 0)
    bodies = bodies_of(lg, "n-blocks")
    for i, hit in enumerate(args["hits"]):
        older, newer = near_kept(lg, i, width + NEAR_SPARE)
        older = [r for r in older if str(r.get("hash") or "") in bodies]
        newer = [r for r in newer if str(r.get("hash") or "") in bodies]
        own = own_history(older + newer, bodies)
        older = [r for r in older if int(r.get("seq") or 0) not in own][:width]
        newer = [r for r in newer if int(r.get("seq") or 0) not in own][:width]
        hit["before"] = [neighbour(r, bodies) for r in reversed(older)]
        hit["after"] = [neighbour(r, bodies) for r in newer]
    emit([answer(call_id, name, search_payload(args))])

if phase == "read-id":
    h = str(args.get("id") or "")
    cands = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in rows(lg, "r-cand")
                    if str(r.get("hash") or "").startswith(h)})
    if not cands:
        refuse(call_id, name, "not_found", "no block of this wall has the id #" + h[:12])
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or "")
    emit([lstore([("r-wall", sel("wall", WALL_COLS, visible({"hash": {"in": cands}}),
                                 [("seq", "asc")])),
                  ("r-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash", "body"], {"hash": {"in": cands}}))]
                 + marks_reads(turn, cands), "read-id-2", call_id, carry(name, args))])

if phase == "read-id-2":
    # Only the rows this round may see name the block, its appearances and its
    # candidates (GH #925): a block whose every row is hidden is not on this
    # round's wall, and a hidden block sharing the prefix is no ambiguity.
    wall = shown(rows(lg, "r-wall"))
    on_wall = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in wall})
    if not on_wall:
        # A hash the ledger holds but the wall never carried (a system leaf, a
        # summary, a window form) is not a block of this model's turns -- in
        # the same words as an id the ledger never held (read-id).
        refuse(call_id, name, "not_found",
               "no block of this wall has the id #" + str(args.get("id") or "")[:12])
    if len(on_wall) > 1:
        refuse(call_id, name, "ambiguous",
               "the id names more than one block; ask with a longer one",
               {"candidates": ["#" + c[:16] for c in on_wall]})
    h = on_wall[0]
    body = bodies_of(lg, "r-blocks").get(h) or ""
    size = len(body)
    el = element_of(body)
    paged = "offset" in args or "length" in args
    page = None
    if (paged or over_budget(size)) and el is not None and isinstance(el.get("text"), str):
        # A block over the budget, or a page asked for: read in pages (A8).
        start = int(args.get("offset") or 0)
        total = len(el["text"])
        if start > total or (start == total and total > 0):
            refuse(call_id, name, "bad_range",
                   "`offset` lies past the end of the block's text (%d characters)" % total,
                   {"total_chars": total})
        page = page_of(el, h, start, args.get("length"))
        if page is None:
            refuse(call_id, name, "too_large",
                   "not even one character of the block fits the read budget",
                   budget_said({"size": size}))
    elif over_budget(size):
        # A block without a text to page through (paging does not reach it).
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large",
               "the block is larger than the read budget and has no text to read in pages",
               budget_said({"size": size}))
    mine = [r for r in wall if str(r.get("hash") or "") == h]
    window = release_window(lg)
    if window is None:
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large", CUT[name], budget_said({}))
    released = released_hashes(window, [h])
    entry = entry_of(mine[0], page[0] if page else el)
    entry["appearances"] = len(mine)
    entry["released"] = h in released
    if page:
        said = budget_said(dict(page[1], blocks=[entry], size=len(canon(page[0]))))
        out = [answer(call_id, name, said)]
    else:
        out = [answer(call_id, name, {"blocks": [entry], "size": size})]
    ops = reread_ops(released, rows(lg, "r-mine"))
    if ops:
        out.append(lstore(ops, "reread", call_id, ""))
    emit(out)

if phase == "read-turns":
    # A bound whose turn holds only rows this round may not see is a turn this
    # wall never had (GH #925); the range is bounded by the rows it may see.
    found = shown(rows(lg, "r-turns"))
    first, last = str(args.get("from_turn") or ""), str(args.get("to_turn") or "")
    head = [r for r in found if str(r.get("turn_id") or "") == first]
    tail = [r for r in found if str(r.get("turn_id") or "") == last]
    missing = [t for t, rs in ((first, head), (last, tail)) if not rs]
    if missing:
        refuse(call_id, name, "not_found",
               "no turn of this wall has the id " + ", ".join(sorted(set(missing))))
    lo = min(int(r.get("seq") or 0) for r in head)
    hi = max(int(r.get("seq") or 0) for r in tail)
    if lo > hi:
        refuse(call_id, name, "bad_range", "`from_turn` lies after `to_turn` on the wall")
    sessions = sorted({str(r.get("session_id") or "") for r in head + tail})
    at_hi = max(str(r.get("at") or "") for r in tail)
    args = dict(args, lo=lo, hi=hi, at_hi=at_hi,
                session=sessions[0] if len(sessions) == 1 else "")
    emit([lstore([("r-range", range_rows(args))], "read-range", call_id, carry(name, args))])

if phase == "read-range":
    got = span_of(args, rows(lg, "r-range"))
    # The bound counts the rows this round may see (GH #925, OR-BD-74): a
    # range with more of them than `scan_budget` is refused, naming the count
    # the same range without hidden rows names -- one more than the budget.
    # Hidden rows that fill the read leave open how many visible ones follow:
    # the range is read once more, to the row bound. A range still not read
    # whole there is refused in the cut form, without a count: the rows it
    # may see up to the bound were 2B + 1 - hidden (closing review I-2).
    span = shown(got)
    bound = ROWS_MAX if args.get("rows_max") else SCAN_BUDGET
    if len(span) > SCAN_BUDGET:
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large",
               "the turn range holds more blocks than one read may; ask for fewer turns",
               budget_said({"block_count_at_least": SCAN_BUDGET + 1}))
    if len(got) > bound:
        if not args.get("rows_max"):
            args = dict(args, rows_max=True)
            emit([lstore([("r-range", range_rows(args))], "read-range", call_id,
                         carry(name, args))])
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large", CUT[name], budget_said({}))
    if not span:
        refuse(call_id, name, "not_found", "the turn range holds no block")
    hashes = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in span})
    emit([lstore([("r-range", range_rows(args)),
                  ("r-chars", sel("blocks", ["hash", "chars"], {"hash": {"in": hashes}}))],
                 "read-range-2", call_id, carry(name, args))])

if phase == "read-range-2":
    span = shown(span_of(args, rows(lg, "r-range")))
    if not span:
        refuse(call_id, name, "not_found", "the turn range holds no block")
    chars = {str(r.get("hash") or ""): int(r.get("chars") or 0) for r in rows(lg, "r-chars")}
    raw = sum(chars.get(str(r.get("hash") or ""), 0) for r in span)
    if READ_BUDGET is not None and raw > RAW_FACTOR * READ_BUDGET:
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large",
               "the turn range is many times larger than the read budget; ask for fewer turns",
               budget_said({"raw_size": raw, "block_count": len(span)}))
    hashes = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in span})
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or "")
    emit([lstore([("r-range", range_rows(args)),
                  ("r-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash", "body"], {"hash": {"in": hashes}}))]
                 + marks_reads(turn, hashes), "read-range-3", call_id, carry(name, args))])

if phase == "read-range-3":
    span = shown(span_of(args, rows(lg, "r-range")))
    bodies = bodies_of(lg, "r-blocks")
    own = own_history(span, bodies)
    kept = [r for r in span if int(r.get("seq") or 0) not in own]
    size = size_of(bodies.get(str(r.get("hash") or ""), "") for r in kept)
    if over_budget(size):
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large",
               "the turn range is larger than the read budget; ask for fewer turns,"
               " or read a block by its id, in pages",
               budget_said({"size": size, "block_count": len(kept)}))
    window = release_window(lg)
    if window is None:
        refuse(call_id, name, "too_large", CUT[name], budget_said({}))
    released = released_hashes(window, sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in kept}))
    entries = []
    for r in kept:
        e = entry_of(r, element_of(bodies.get(str(r.get("hash") or ""))))
        e["released"] = str(r.get("hash") or "") in released
        entries.append(e)
    out = [answer(call_id, name, {"blocks": entries, "size": size,
                                  "skipped_history": len(span) - len(kept),
                                  "from_turn": args.get("from_turn"),
                                  "to_turn": args.get("to_turn")})]
    ops = reread_ops(released, rows(lg, "r-mine"))
    if ops:
        out.append(lstore(ops, "reread", call_id, ""))
    emit(out)

if phase == "outline":
    wall, marks = rows(lg, "o-wall"), rows(lg, "o-marks")
    bound = ROWS_MAX if args.get("rows_max") else SCAN_BUDGET
    # The outline reaches the newest `scan_budget` rows this round may see
    # (GH #925, OR-BD-74): hidden rows that fill the first read send it once
    # more, to the row bound.
    if not args.get("rows_max") and (
            (len(wall) > SCAN_BUDGET and len(shown(wall)) < len(wall))
            or (len(marks) >= SCAN_BUDGET and len(shown(marks)) < len(marks))):
        emit([outline_reads(dict(args, rows_max=True))])
    seen, noted = shown(wall), shown(marks)
    # Where the row bound leaves open which are the newest `scan_budget` rows
    # -- or `topic` marks -- the round may see, the outline answers in the cut
    # form: the sessions out of what it read counted the hidden rows (closing
    # review I-2). The topics come out of the newest `scan_budget` marks it
    # may see, as without hidden ones: one hidden mark among 15 used to bring
    # all 15 in and a topic the budget's ten do not open (OR-BD-86 driver).
    if args.get("rows_max") and ((len(seen) <= SCAN_BUDGET and len(wall) > bound)
                                 or (len(noted) < SCAN_BUDGET and len(marks) >= bound)):
        out = {"sessions": [], "truncated_scan": True, "detail": CUT[name]}
        if args.get("since"):
            out["since"] = args["since"]
        emit([answer(call_id, name, out)])
    # Sessions, turns and topics out of the rows and `topic` marks this round
    # may see (GH #925): a hidden mark neither opens nor closes a topic. The
    # newest `scan_budget` rows, those of them whose turn lies at or after
    # `since` (OR-KF-21); cut short only where the next row read is one too.
    span = seen[:SCAN_BUDGET]
    wall = list(reversed([r for r in span if inside(args, r)]))
    truncated = len(seen) > SCAN_BUDGET and inside(args, seen[SCAN_BUDGET])
    window = noted[:SCAN_BUDGET]
    marks = list(reversed(window))
    if len(window) >= SCAN_BUDGET:
        # The marks read are full: the mark that named the open topic may
        # lie before them (A7). The newest one that says something, when it
        # does lie there and does not end its topic, opens the list.
        low = min(int(m.get("seq") or 0) for m in window)
        seed = next(iter(shown(rows(lg, "o-seed"))), None)
        t = topic_of((seed or {}).get("value"))
        if seed is not None and int(seed.get("seq") or 0) < low and t and t[0] != "end":
            marks = [seed] + marks
    emit([answer(call_id, name, outline_answer(wall, marks, args.get("since"), truncated))])

park("store answer in unknown phase %r -- dropped" % phase)

scan_budget.description: The most wall rows the round may see that one `history_search` reads, newest first (and one outline); a search that stops there says `truncated_scan` with `cut_by` `scan_budget` and answers with the hits up to that point, a turn range with more such rows is refused with `too_large`; `released` of a `history_read` is decided by the newest this many `release`/`pin` marks of its blocks the round may see. Rows of other rounds count toward no budget, but every read stops at twice this many rows in all (GH #925, GH #931). Where that row bound leaves the answer open, the call answers in the cut form and shows nothing it read: a search `hits` [], `cut_by` `scan_budget`, a `detail` and no `scanned` or `total_hits`; a `history_read` `too_large` with a `detail` and no `block_count_at_least`; an outline no sessions. The form is the same on every wall that reaches the bound, so there rows of other rounds move one bit per call and never a count; it takes at least this many of them among the first twice this + 1 rows one read meets (of a read's `release`/`pin` marks, more than this many among their newest twice this), or for the neighbours of a search with `context` at least this / hits - `context` - 3 of the hit's session on one side. Below the bound every number an answer carries counts rows the round may see, but where a page ends and how long a read takes still depend on rows of other rounds (GH #932). The round loses that call's answer; a narrower `since`/`until` brings it back (OR-BD-86).

time_budget_ms.description: The most time one `history_search` spends, from the call on; a match that runs past it is interrupted and the search answers with the hits up to that point (`truncated_scan`, `cut_by` `time_budget`). Below `external_timeout_ms`, so the answer always comes before the runner would kill the child.

page_rows.description: The wall rows the round may see that one page of a search matches per ledger round trip; a search stops at the page that fills its `limit` (`stopped_at_limit`).

place.description: GH #1279: the place of the person (a town, a locale) the judge context names as `judge.place` and the seed's fact line as `place:`; the composition renders it from the profile. "" (the default) names no place.

timezone.description: GH #1279: the IANA zone (`Europe/Berlin`) `judge.now` is given in (`iso` with its offset, `weekday`, `timezone`). "" (the default) or an unknown zone is UTC, the latter said on stderr.

now_utc.description: GH #1279: a fixed instant (RFC 3339, UTC) for `judge.now`, the test override of its wall-clock read. "" (the default) reads the clock.

seed_entries_max.description: The most session and until notes one `seed` carries in its `Notes:` line -- the best ranked, `priority` first (0 first), then the youngest, shown oldest first; the rest stays out of the seed and is said on stderr (the live feed's facts still count every note). 0 (the default) carries every note.

seed_anchor.description: The persona's anchor, one `developer` line a `seed` ends on -- after the turns and a held `hint`, right before a held `wind_down` (the end of the call stays last), in the head before the turns only with `seed_anchor_first` "1" (GH #1402); counted in the seed's budget. "" (the default) adds nothing.

seed_anchor_first.description: #1402: "1" puts `seed_anchor` at the end of the seed's head (after the facts, a held `identity` line and the notes), in front of the turns, instead of into the tail; "0" (the default) keeps it in the tail. Without an anchor nothing moves.

seed_renew_line.description: #1402: the set's wait line of a renewed session -- on an `in_seed_ask` whose `hop.reason` is `renew` or `recover` the LAST `developer` line of the seed, after the anchor and a held `wind_down`; never on `start`; counted in the seed's budget. "" (the default) adds nothing.

topic_aging.description: GH #1436: "1" lets the topic age -- one rule in `./history` (the topic handed to the route stamp, the judge and a seed) and `./policy` (the topic of a call's live feed): it frames no turn of a call opened after it was named, none of a session it was not last named in, and none once `topic_age_turns` turns passed without a renewed mention. "0" (the default) = the reads and answers as before, byte for byte.

topic_age_turns.description: GH #1436: with `topic_aging` "1" the turns without a renewed mention after which a topic frames no turn any more; counted by the person's rows on the wall (one per turn), not by marks.

topic_age_rows.description: GH #1436: with `topic_aging` "1" the bound of the read that counts the turns since the topic was named (the person's rows, newest first); a read that comes back full without reaching the naming counts as `topic_age_turns` turns. Keep it above `topic_age_turns`.

wellbeing_line.description: D38 V2 (GH #1451): "1" opens a call with the open wellbeing of the day as one line of data -- the newest fact of the day with predicate `health` (or `needs` with stance `unfulfilled`) at `wellbeing_min_confidence` or above, `{state: open, subject, predicate, claim, fact_seq}` -- in the seed and its facts state, and the seed that carried it books a `wellbeing` mark `{state: closed}`: asked after once. The same function `wellbeing_line` as `./policy`. "0" = the seed as it was.

wellbeing_min_confidence.description: D38 V2 (GH #1451): the least confidence of a fact that opens the wellbeing line (a mark without one passes); only with `wellbeing_line` "1".

wellbeing_rows.description: D38 V2 (GH #1451): with `wellbeing_line` "1" the bound of the seed's read of the day's `fact` and `wellbeing` marks, newest first.

notes_latest_per_item.description: D38 V1 (GH #1451, review o15-Rv1 m2): the window's knob of `./policy` in the seed -- "1" reads `notes.item` and the seed (and `call_facts`) carries only the youngest note of one `(source, item)`; a note without an item stays. "0" (the default) the seed of before.

session_id.description: on `seed`: the `session_id` of the `seed_ask`, given back unchanged with `call_id` and `renewal_n` (the voice cell refuses a seed without them); on `call_facts`: the `session_id` of the `in_call_end`, given back with `call_id` (#1369)

description.purpose: The model reads its own wall (GH #893): `history_search` (phrase, exact text or regular expression, newest first, with time, kind, limit and neighbour bounds, page by page and within a time budget), `history_read` (one block by its id `#<12 hex>`, or a turn range, whole or refused with `too_large`) and `history_outline` (sessions with their turn ranges and the topics their `topic` marks opened and closed, OR-KY-71), answered out of this hive's ledger alone. The model's own `history_*` calls and their answers are no hits and no blocks of a range. A read of a block TRIM released writes one `reread` mark per block and turn. Every row of `wall` and `marks` it reads passes the audience gate of the round the call is served in (`context.audience_set`, GH #925): a row whose audience does not hold the round, or that has none, is no hit, no neighbour, no block of a range, no id and no session, turn or topic of the outline -- an id or a turn the round may not see is `not_found` in the words an unknown one gets. A `reread` mark carries the round's audience. Since GH #1304 it also answers the internal lane `in_turns_ask` of `talky/route` (OR-EP-4): the person's last `n` turns of the running generation and round -- wall rows of kind `user` only, never the running turn (`context.turn_id`), oldest first, within `budget_tokens` (at most 4000, 1500 at or below 0 or without one) by the token-estimate block, the oldest dropped first. Since #1279 it builds the judge context out of the same wall: `in_turns_ask` with `turns_ask.judge: true` answers `turns` unchanged plus `judge` (the running generation's last `n` turns of both roles, the newest named topic, the screen topics, `now`, `place`), `in_seed_ask` answers one `seed` (the round's newest turns of both roles within 8192 tokens behind one fact line, the held seed line last), and `in_screen_topics` / `in_seed_line` keep one `state` row each.
description.use_when: Inside the curator only; the parent routes `hop.tool_name` with the prefix `history_` to the hive's `in_history_call` lane and takes `tool_result` back into its collector's `in_tool`.
description.not_in_scope: No model, no embedding, no ranking: deterministic ledger reads. No other model's wall -- the ledger is this hive's. The schemas the model is offered are the curator's menu answer (`HISTORY_SCHEMAS` in `./schemas`, spliced into `CURATOR_OFFER`), not this cell's.
description.emits_meaning: tool_result: the answer to one call, one `tool_result` turn under its call id, the text a JSON object; a refusal names its code in the text and in `hop.error_code` (bad_arguments, bad_pattern, bad_range, not_found, ambiguous, too_large, unknown_tool, ledger_error, missing_audience -- a round that declares no audience, refused before anything is read; empty on an answer). A search cut short is an answer (`truncated_scan`, `cut_by` `scan_budget` or `time_budget`; `stopped_at_limit`). lstore: ledger reads, and the `reread` marks. turns: the answer to one `in_turns_ask`, exactly one, `{messages: [], turns: [{turn_id, text}], truncated}`; `hop.refused` `no_round` (no round, nothing read) or `bad_arguments` (`n` below 1), `hop.degraded` `store` (a refused ledger read), both absent on an answer. seed: the answer to one `in_seed_ask`, exactly one, `{messages: [{role, text}], est_tokens, judge}` -- `messages` one `developer` fact line, a `developer` line `Notes: ...` of the session and until notes, the turns as `user`/`assistant` and the inner turns as `developer` lines `(<kind>) <text>`, the held `in_seed_line` last as `developer`; `est_tokens` by the estimate the budget counts with; the facts it carried are written as `seed_facts:<call>` for the live feed; `hop.call_id`, `hop.renewal_n` given back; `hop.refused` `no_round` or `hop.degraded` `store` with `messages: []`. call_facts (#1369): the answer to one `in_call_end`, exactly one, `{messages: [], call_id, session_id, seed_used, facts: [{source, id, text}], delegations: [{turn_id, text}]}` -- read only, the call's `seed_facts:<call>` stays; `hop.call_id`, `hop.session_id` given back; `hop.refused` `no_round`/`no_call` or `hop.degraded` `store` with `seed_used` false and empty lists.
description.consumes_meaning: in_history_call (one `tool_call` turn, `hop.tool_call_id`, `hop.tool_name`, the round in `context.audience_set`) and the ledger's answers to its phases (search-rows, search-page, search-near, search-near-2, read-id, read-id-2, read-turns, read-range, read-range-2, read-range-3, outline, reread). in_turns_ask (`turns_ask: {n, budget_tokens}`, the round in `context.audience_set`, `context.session_id`, `context.turn_id`) and the ledger's answers to its phases (turns-rows, turns-blocks). in_seed_ask (`hop.call_id`/`context.call_id`, `hop.renewal_n`, the round in `context.audience_set`) and its phases (seed-rows, seed-blocks); in_screen_topics (`topics: [{name, purpose, candidates?}]`) and in_seed_line (`{call_id|session_id, kind, text}`), each one `state` write (phase judge-write), answered by nothing. in_call_end (#1369: `hop.call_id`, `hop.session_id`, the round in `context.audience_set`) and its phases (call-facts-rows, call-facts-blocks). in_turns_ask with `context.delta` "1" (a delta of a voice turn, under the call's id) reads the round's rows whatever their session, like in_seed_ask.
